front_line: American-made battlefield robotics at the point where validation must become scale.
thesis: Watchlist. The Army win is real and the asymmetry is real, but you are paying platform prices for a business that has proven it can ship units — not make money — while a near-forced dilution clock ticks. This moves to Open on the one combination every agent named: gross margin sustained above 25% for two straight quarters alongside disclosure of a firm, funded multi-year SRR contract — ideally at a price no higher than the base case.
moat: One emerging regulatory/qualification advantage, but zero pricing power today (3% margin) resting on a possibly-unfunded selection and near-total customer concentration.
risks: Q1 FY2027 burned $91.3M FCF in a single quarter — nearly all of FY2026's $95.8M — leaving roughly 1.4 quarters of runway and a near-certain dilutive raise.

image.query: A solitary crimson geometric wedge breaking through a dark wall of distorted signal static, then multiplying behind the barrier into hundreds of smaller coordinated forms arranged in a precise expanding formation. The surrounding landscape shifts from fragmented chaos into an engineered grid, symbolizing battlefield validation becoming industrial scale and networked autonomy. Moody graphite, gunmetal, ash, and muted military green with one deep red accent. Cinematic lighting, volumetric haze, sophisticated abstract editorial art, premium financial-magazine aesthetic, high contrast, dramatic depth, visually striking but restrained.
